ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the combined image, inside the paper frame of <image1> there are 2 long horizontal strips, 1 black circle, and 1 plus sign; inside the paper frame of <image2> there are 5 black circles and 3 plus signs; the crown template of <image3> is composed of 1 horizontal strip, 4 black circles, and 1 plus sign. Reasoning: Lisa wants to make 7 identical crowns, so in total she needs 7 horizontal strips, 28 black circles, and 7 plus signs. Suppose x sheets of image1-type paper and y sheets of image2-type paper are cut, then the constraints are 2x >= 7, x + 5y >= 28, x + 3y >= 7, and x + y must be minimized. From 2x >= 7, we get x >= 4. When x = 4, the circle constraint gives 4 + 5y >= 28, so y >= 5; at this time the number of plus signs is 4 + 3*5 = 19, which is enough. A total of 4 + 5 = 9 sheets are needed. If the total number of sheets is less than 9, then under x >= 4, at most 8 sheets cannot satisfy 28 circles, so 9 is the minimum value.

method.method_draft: Read the parts available from each sheet type: image1 shows one sheet containing 2 long horizontal strips, 1 black circle, and 1 plus sign; image2 shows one sheet containing 5 black circles and 3 plus signs. Read the crown template in image3 as needing 1 long strip, 4 black circles, and 1 plus sign. From the text, Lisa needs 7 identical crowns. Therefore total required parts are 7 strips, 28 circles, and 7 plus signs. Let x be the number of image1 sheets and y the number of image2 sheets. Set up the constraints 2x >= 7, x + 5y >= 28, and x + 3y >= 7, then minimize x + y over nonnegative integers. Since 2x >= 7 forces x >= 4, and with x = 4 the circle constraint gives 4 + 5y >= 28 so y >= 5. This gives 4 + 5 = 9 sheets, and the plus signs are enough because 4 + 15 >= 7.

Image3 shows every crown has exactly one long horizontal strip, and only image1 sheets contain long strips; image2 sheets contain circles and plus signs but no strips. Since image1 has 2 strips per sheet and 7 crowns need 7 strips, at least 4 image1 sheets are unavoidable. Four image1 sheets provide 8 strips, 4 circles, and 4 plus signs. Compare this with the visual crown requirement from image3: 7 crowns need 28 circles and 7 plus signs. After using 4 image1 sheets, Lisa is still short 24 circles and 3 plus signs. Image2 supplies 5 circles and 3 plus signs per sheet, so the circle shortage requires at least 5 image2 sheets. Check construction: 4 image1 sheets and 5 image2 sheets give 8 strips, 29 circles, and 19 plus signs, enough for 7 crowns. Thus the minimum is 4 + 5 = 9 sheets.
